reasoning_summary: The simulated problem matches the question. In every run, cylinder_diameter 0.01 matches the patch extents (0.01 m in x and y). The inlet velocity of 0.15 m/s was measured at the inlet as uniform (ux_nonuniformity 0.0, uy_max_abs 0.0). Re is 100 in both case and spec, and 0.15*0.01/1.5e-5 gives 100. The reference quantities magUInf 0.15, lRef 0.01, Aref 0.0001 and rhoInf 1.2 match the spec. The cylinder wall is noSlip.

The domain is set up as an unbounded stream. Blockage is 0.0125 in R0, falling to 0.0083333 in R4 and 0.00625 in R2. Cd moves monotonically with domain size: 1.3311 (R0), 1.3251 (R4), 1.3226 (R2). The estimated domain uncertainty is 1.23% for Cd and 0.79% for St, both within budget.

R2 has checkMesh_ok=false and a coarser mesh, so its domain signal is confounded with mesh coarsening. This is not blocking. The mesh_quality figures recorded for R2 equal R0's (max_non_orthogonality_deg 43.313, max_skewness 0.53384). R4 has a clean mesh and shows the same trend. A coarser mesh would also be expected to push Cd the same way as the R0-to-R5 mesh trend, so the domain estimate is more likely conservative than optimistic.

The quantities are consistent across independent runs. R0 and R3 agree on St (0.16344 vs 0.16357) and on Cd (1.3311 vs 1.3275). The mesh-refined runs R5 and R1 agree on Cd (1.3349 and 1.3349) and are within 0.26% of each other on St (0.16443 and 0.16486). The R0 St frequency resolution of 0.013333 is coarse, but the FFT and zero-crossing values agree (0.16344 vs 0.16343) and match the other runs. The 12 stationary cycles with drift of 8.2286e-05 show the averaging window is stationary.

The combined uncertainties are 1.87% for Cd and 1.59% for St, against a 3% tolerance. I found no recorded evidence of a mismatch between what was simulated and what was asked, so I have no field-specific blocking concern.
